project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used to provide technical assistance and training to manage solid-waste management programs of 30 communities located in the New Hampshire Lakes Region. This project will provide technical assistance and training to solid-waste operators in order to reduce the quantity and toxicity of their solid-waste stream, and lower the costs associated with solid-waste management. This multi-pronged approach to education and training for solid-waste operators, community leaders, town committees, local businesses and residents in New Hampshires Lakes Region will improve the cost-effectiveness of waste recycling. It will also reduce the quantity of recyclable and hazardous materials entering the municipal waste stream, and reduce costs to municipalities with smaller volumes of waste and lower overhead costs. Positive outcomes include increased opportunities for better contract pricing and long-term protection of the Lakes Regions water quality (the region contains 40% of New Hampshires surface waters).

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to finance water and sewer systems improvements for Deer Estates Cooperative in Milan, N.H. The Cooperative is a non-profit, resident-owned community of manufactured homes consisting of 20 residential units located on a nine-acre parcel where municipal water and sewer services are not available. Due to age and deterioration, the Cooperative regularly deals with septic maintenance and usage concerns, and the negative impacts to abutting infrastructure. With each breakage and repair, bacteria and/or pathogens enter the system. Improvements include replacement of water mains, booster pump station components and on-site septic systems. Failed septics are causing concerns for residents and surrounding bodies of water given the high groundwater table. This project addresses a public health and sanitary problem that affects 29 people.

The School is an open-enrollment public charter school for high-school students in grades 9-12, offering alternative education for students with differentiated learning and behavioral needs who struggle in the traditional classroom setting. Ledyard provides hands-on, specialized curriculum for its students at half the cost of a traditional public school, and has built a solid reputation by graduating an average of nearly 40 kids a year. The campus location and proximity to community services is essential to the programs sustainability, as its near public transportation access, a library, a sports facility, and internship and workforce opportunities with local business partnerships. The school was approved by the NH State Board of Education in 2007, and operates with oversight by a Board of Trustees and the New Hampshire Department of Education. Additional funding is being provided by seller financing and the applicant.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to install an elevator at the newly renovated town office building in Bristol, N.H. The facility houses municipal services including administrative, public safety, highway, recreation and public assistance. The former municipal building is adjacent to a 100-year floodplain. Due to the increased severity of flood events, the town decided to purchase and rehabilitate a building that is further away from the floodplain. Bristol is located in a 2019 FEMA declared disaster area. This project is essential in meeting accessibility standards and providing both staff and the public access to all levels of the building as well as ensuring continued operations during flood events.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide financial and technical assistance to organizations in Millinocket and Patten, Maine, to develop their capacity and ability to undertake projects related to community and economic development. However, this project is unique in its specific focus on the tourism and outdoor recreation sector. This timing of this proposal is particularly important as COVID-19 closed the regional tourism economy in mid-March, leaving area businesses reeling. This coordinated and strategic capacity-building project will lay a stronger foundation for the re-opening and continued diversification of the Katahdin regional economy. The entire Katahdin Region has benefitted from increased interest in its well-being and groups have spent considerable time engaging the public in ideas and visions for the future. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to make wastewater improvements which include decommissioning two sludge lagoons and installing a solar field for the Town of Epping, NH. With the completion of recent facility upgrades, the lagoons are no longer needed. Decommissioning of the unlined lagoons is necessary as they are considered a health hazard and in violation of federal, state, and local laws due to the resulting contamination of groundwater and elevated nitrogen levels. The primary driving force behind the solar project is cost, more specifically the capital and O&M costs, but also the energy cost savings for the Town as the wastewater facility is its single largest energy user. This project will benefit 921 users by relieving a health and safety concern as well as reducing energy consumption and reusing the lagoons land for an environmentally conscious project.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used for a preliminary engineering report and environmental report to develop a new well source. The town has two wells, one of which is often contaminated and not usable. Based on engineering design standards for water works, a minimum of two sources of groundwater should be provided. naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide technical assistance and training to direct solid waste programs in 50 northernmost communities in New Hampshire. The Council will work with community leaders and waste management personnel to analyze current waste practices, identify alternatives that increase recycling, and become more efficient and cost effective. Through promoting best management practices, the amount of waste sent to landfills and cost of disposal will be reduced and hazardous wastes will be removed from the waste stream, therefore minimizing pollution of water resources and extending the lives of their regional landfills.

borrower_name: Upper Valley Lake Sunapee Regional Planning Commission
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to direct solid waste programs in 24 targeted communities in New Hampshire. The project goals are to increase knowledge and awareness of toxic products, proper hazardous waste disposal, safety and efficiency of municipal facilities, and recycling and reuse of materials. These goals will be accomplished through implementation of a pilot project at long-term care facility to create a guide for green cleaning; hazardous waste training and workshops for household hazardous waste coordinators and managers; operational training for transfer station attendants and town officials on difficult to manage items such as universal waste and food scraps; providing nontoxic cleaning and personal care product public outreach; and implementation of a compost pilot project at three to five elementary schools. This project will allow for solid waste management programs to be more effective at protecting the environment and human health and improving municipal operations.
